after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+3z=-1-x \\ 4y=-5z \\ x+6z-3=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=-1 \\ 4y+5z=0 \\ x+6z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(24)-2(-5)+3(0-4) \\  & =24+10-12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -5 & -4 \\ 12 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}24 & 5 & -4 \\ -12 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}-30 \\ -20 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{15}{11} \\ -\frac{10}{11} \\ \frac{8}{11}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-\frac{15}{11},y=-\frac{10}{11},z=\frac{8}{11}.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
content.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y+3z=-1-x \\ 4y=-5z \\ x+6z-3=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=-1 \\ 4y+5z=0 \\ x+6z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(24)-2(-5)+3(0-4) \\  & =24+10-12 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -5 & -4 \\ 12 & 3 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}24 & 5 & -4 \\ -12 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}24 & -12 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{22}[\begin{aligned}-30 \\ -20 \\ 16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{15}{11} \\ -\frac{10}{11} \\ \frac{8}{11}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-\frac{15}{11},y=-\frac{10}{11},z=\frac{8}{11}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Consider a matrix equation $A{B}^{-1}\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $5\times 5$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $5\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${A}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $A{B}^{-1}\,x=d$ by ${A}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A{B}^{-1}\,x & =d \\ {A}^{-1}A{B}^{-1}\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{5}{B}^{-1}\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ {B}^{-1}\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${B}^{-1}\,x={A}^{-1}\,d$ by $B,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{-1}\,x & ={A}^{-1}\,d \\ B{B}^{-1}\,x & =B{A}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{5}\,x & =B{A}^{-1}\,d \\ x & =B{A}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Left-multiply both sides by A: AA^{-1}x=AB^{-1}d. Since AA^{-1}=I, this gives x=AB^{-1}d, which is option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Consider a matrix equation ${A}^{-1}\,x={B}^{-1}\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $5\times 5$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $5\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${A}^{-1}\,x={B}^{-1}\,d$ by $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}\,x & ={B}^{-1}\,d \\ A{A}^{-1}\,x & =A{B}^{-1}\,d \\ {I}_{5}\,x & =A{B}^{-1}\,d \\ x & =A{B}^{-1}\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =0|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-(8-4)+(4-4) \\  & =-4+0 \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$

$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$

decision.explanation: Reorder the equations as x+y+z=2, y-3z=3, and 2x+y+4z=4. The coefficient matrix has rows (1,1,1), (0,1,-3), (2,1,4), and its inverse has rows (-7,3,4), (6,-2,-3), (2,-1,-1). Multiplying by (2,3,4)^T gives (x,y,z)=(11,-6,-3), matching option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+z+x=2 \\ -3z+y=3 \\ 2x+y=4-4z\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ y-3z=3 \\ 2x+y+4z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4+3)-(0+6)+(0-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & 1\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=11,y=-6,z=-3.$

content.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+z+x=2 \\ -3z+y=3 \\ 2x+y=4-4z\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x+y+z=2 \\ y-3z=3 \\ 2x+y+4z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4+3)-(0+6)+(0-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & 3 & 1\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & -4 \\ -6 & 2 & 3 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 3 & 4 \\ 6 & -2 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -6 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=11,y=-6,z=-3.$
